claim: H3K27me3 levels increase with age in wild-type Drosophila muscle tissues.
source: Western blot analysis showed that only H3K27me2/3 were selectively reduced in PRC2 mutants, while other histone markings remained unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blot data from Figure 1—figure supplement 1A shows age-associated increase in H3K27me3 levels in wild-type flies.

claim: H3K27me3 peak profiles remain largely unchanged during adult aging despite increased overall levels.
source: Surprisingly, despite the fact that H3K27me3 levels increased with age, H3K27me3 peak profiles in the aging adult remained largely unchanged (Figure 1A).
evidence: ChIP-seq data from muscle tissues of 3-, 15-, and 30-day-old flies showing comparable peak profiles.

claim: H3K27me3 modification undergoes dramatic gain or loss during Drosophila development.
source: In a sharp contrast, H3K27me3 signals during developmental stages showed dramatic gain or loss (Figure 1B).
evidence: ChIP-seq data from embryo, larvae, and pupae showing dynamic changes in H3K27me3 signals.

claim: Inter-peak genes gain relatively more H3K27me3 modification during aging compared to peak genes.
source: In aging WT flies, despite a genome-wide increase, we noted that inter-peak genes gained relatively more signals than those of peak genes (Figure 1E).
evidence: Bootstrapping analysis showing inter-peak genes gained 36.4% (15d) and 48.4% (30d) signal versus 9.4% (15d) and 13.3% (30d) for peak genes.

claim: H3K27me3 modification during aging has reduced selectivity for peak regions.
source: Modification in flies that were 3d old was predominantly biased at the peaks, with approximately 323% more signals as compared to the inter-peaks (Figure 1G). In contrast, the signals acquired during aging were only about 9% more at the peaks than those at the inter-peaks (Figure 1G), suggesting that there was a dramatic shift in the pattern of H3K27me3 modification in aging.
evidence: Bootstrapping analysis comparing signal distribution between peak and inter-peak regions at different ages.

claim: Pair-wise combinations of PRC2 double mutants in trans-heterozygosity result in stronger effects on H3K27me3-reduction and life-extension.
source: Remarkably, double mutants demonstrated more striking effects on H3K27me3-reduction and life-extension (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Western blot and lifespan data from PRC2 trans-heterozygous double mutants showing enhanced phenotypes.

claim: Only H3K27me2/3 are selectively reduced in PRC2 mutants while other histone markings remain unchanged.
source: Of note, western blot analysis showed that only H3K27me2/3 were selectively reduced in PRC2 mutants, while other histone markings remained unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Western blot analysis of multiple histone modifications showing selective reduction of H3K27me2/3.

claim: Global occupancy of H3K27me3 between WT and age-matched PRC2 mutants is preserved.
source: Interestingly, global occupancy of H3K27me3 between WT and age-matched PRC2 mutants was preserved, as demonstrated by the comparable patterns of peak profiles and genes known to be H3K27me3-modified (pair-wise Pearson correlation coefficients ≥ 0.77) (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C)
evidence: Pearson correlation analysis showing high correlation coefficients between WT and PRC2 mutants.

claim: In PRC2 mutants at 3d, H3K27me3 signals become more likely to coalesce into peak regions.
source: In PRC2 mutants at 3d where H3K27me3 bulk levels were substantially decreased, interestingly, the signals became more likely to coalesce into the peak regions (Figure 3C, see Figure 3—figure supplement 1E for escc289 E(z)c239).
evidence: Bootstrapping analysis showing relative enrichment of signals at peak regions in young PRC2 mutants.

claim: Age-associated drifting of H3K27me3 is dampened in PRC2 mutants.
source: More strikingly, age-associated shift in H3K27me3 modification that occurred in WT was now dampened in mutants (Figure 3E, see Figure 3—figure supplement 1G for escc289 E(z)c239).
evidence: Scatter plot analysis showing reduced age-associated changes in H3K27me3 in PRC2 mutants compared to WT.

claim: Glycolytic process and related pathways are enriched among genes upregulated in PRC2 mutants.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis revealed that the 'glycolytic process' and closely related pathways were highlighted for genes upregulated (Figure 5A)
evidence: GO analysis of RNA-seq data from PRC2 mutants showing enrichment of glycolytic genes.

claim: Oxidation-reduction process is enriched among genes downregulated in PRC2 mutants.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis revealed that the 'glycolytic process' and closely related pathways were highlighted for genes upregulated (Figure 5A), while the 'oxidation-reduction process' was enriched for genes downregulated (Figure 5A).
evidence: GO analysis of RNA-seq data showing enrichment of oxidation-reduction genes among downregulated genes.

claim: Tpi and Pgi glycolytic genes are upregulated in both muscle and head tissues across individual long-lived PRC2 mutants.
source: We then extended RNA-seq analysis to the heads, and further narrowed down to two glycolytic genes, Tpi and Pgi, whose expressions were upregulated in both tissue types across individual long-lived PRC2 mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: RNA-seq data from both muscle and head tissues showing consistent upregulation of Tpi and Pgi.

claim: Genes downregulated with age in WT are mainly enriched in carbohydrate metabolism and energy production.
source: Moreover, RNA-seq analyses of WT animals revealed that, although aging might exert a much broader effect on the changes of the transcriptome, genes downregulated with age were mainly enriched in carbohydrate metabolism and energy production (Figure 5C).
evidence: GO analysis of age-dependent gene expression changes showing enrichment in metabolic pathways.

claim: Genes related to glycolysis/gluconeogenesis show age-associated transcriptional decrease in WT.
source: In particular, we noted a transcriptional decline of genes related to glycolysis/gluconeogenesis in old animals (Figure 5D).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis of KEGG-annotated glycolysis/gluconeogenesis genes showing decreased expression with age.

claim: Tpi and Pgi mRNA levels are increased in PRC1 mutants.
source: In addition to PRC2 mutants, we attested the transcriptional increase of these two glycolytic genes in Su(z)2c433, a long-lived PRC1 mutant (Figure 5H).
evidence: qRT-PCR data showing increased Tpi and Pgi expression in PRC1 mutants.

claim: utx null mutants display a further increase of H3K27me3 compared to age-matched WT.
source: The Drosophila Utx gene has been previously implicated in catalyzing the removal of methyl groups from H3K27me3 (Smith et al., 2008); a null mutation, utxc499 (Supplementary file 2), displayed a further increase of H3K27me3 compared to age-matched WT (Figure 5E and I, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Western blot and ChIP-qPCR data showing increased H3K27me3 in utx mutants.

claim: Flies lacking utx have a significantly shortened lifespan to about 70% that of WT animals.
source: Flies lacking utx were viable, but detailed characterization indicated a significantly shortened lifespan, to about 70% that of WT animals (Figure 5J).
evidence: Lifespan assay data showing reduced survival in utx mutants.

claim: Expression of Tpi and Pgi is further decreased in utx mutants concomitant with increased H3K27me3.
source: Concomitant with an increase in H3K27me3 modification, expression of both Tpi and Pgi was further decreased (Figure 5K).
evidence: qRT-PCR data showing decreased Tpi and Pgi expression in utx mutants.

claim: Lactate levels are significantly decreased during normal aging in WT animals.
source: In particular, lactate, a specific indicator for anaerobic glycolysis (Schurr and Payne, 2007), was significantly decreased during normal aging in WT animals but became elevated in PRC2 mutants (Figure 6E).
evidence: Untargeted metabolomics data showing decreased lactate levels with age in WT.

claim: Lactate levels are elevated in PRC2 mutants.
source: In particular, lactate, a specific indicator for anaerobic glycolysis (Schurr and Payne, 2007), was significantly decreased during normal aging in WT animals but became elevated in PRC2 mutants (Figure 6E).
evidence: Untargeted metabolomics data showing increased lactate levels in PRC2 mutants.

claim: Metabolites related to citric acid cycle remain unchanged between WT and PRC2 mutants.
source: Of note, metabolites related to citric acid cycle remained unchanged between WT and mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Metabolomic analysis showing no significant changes in citric acid cycle metabolites.

claim: Glycolytic metabolites exhibit an age-associated decline in WT that is partially reversed by PRC2-deficiency.
source: This experiment demonstrated that while the level of labeled glucose was similar (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C), specific metabolites (Figure 6G) and the glycolytic pathway as a whole (Figure 6H) exhibited an age-associated decline; strikingly, the extent of decline was partially reversed by PRC2-deficiency.
evidence: 13C-glucose metabolic flux data showing age-associated decline in glycolysis that is reduced in PRC2 mutants.

claim: Glucose levels between WT and PRC2 mutants have no significant difference.
source: While the overall glucose levels between WT and mutants had no significant difference (Figure 7A)
evidence: Glucose measurement showing no significant difference between genotypes.

claim: Pyruvate levels are increased in PRC2 mutants.
source: pyruvate was increased in mutants (Figure 7A).
evidence: Pyruvate assay showing increased levels in PRC2 mutants.

claim: The ratio of NADPH/NADP+ is slightly decreased in PRC2 mutants.
source: On the other hand, the ratio of NADPH/NADP+, an indicator of the PPP, foliate metabolism, and malic enzyme (Fan et al., 2014) was even slightly decreased in mutants (Figure 7B).
evidence: NADPH/NADP+ ratio measurement showing slight decrease in PRC2 mutants.

claim: ATP levels are decreased with age but increased in PRC2 mutants.
source: Our data showed that ATP, NADH/NAD+, and GSH/(GSH +GSSG) ratio were decreased with age but increased in mutants (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: ATP measurements showing age-associated decrease in WT and increase in PRC2 mutants.

claim: NADH/NAD+ ratio is decreased with age but increased in PRC2 mutants.
source: Our data showed that ATP, NADH/NAD+, and GSH/(GSH +GSSG) ratio were decreased with age but increased in mutants (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: NADH/NAD+ ratio measurements showing age-associated decrease in WT and increase in PRC2 mutants.

claim: GSH/(GSH+GSSG) ratio is decreased with age but increased in PRC2 mutants.
source: Our data showed that ATP, NADH/NAD+, and GSH/(GSH +GSSG) ratio were decreased with age but increased in mutants (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: Glutathione ratio measurements showing age-associated decrease in WT and increase in PRC2 mutants.

claim: PRC2 mutants have better climbing mobility at 30d of age compared to WT.
source: Analysis of climbing of young (3d) and aged (30d) animals demonstrated that although WT and mutants at 3d behaved similarly, PRC2 mutants at 30d of age had better locomotion (Figure 7E).
evidence: Climbing assay data showing improved mobility in aged PRC2 mutants.

claim: PRC2 mutants have substantially enhanced resistance to oxidative stress.
source: We observed substantially enhanced resistance to oxidation in mutants (Figure 7F).
evidence: H2O2 stress assay showing increased survival in PRC2 mutants.

claim: Tpi deficiency partially mitigates the longevity phenotype in PRC2 mutants.
source: Analysis of lifespan exhibited that Tpi deficiency partially mitigated the longevity phenotype in PRC2 mutants (Figure 8A).
evidence: Lifespan assay showing reduced lifespan extension in PRC2 mutants with Tpi deficiency.

claim: Tpi deficiency attenuates resistance to ROS and climbing mobility in PRC2 mutants.
source: Traits related to adult fitness, including resistance to ROS and climbing mobility, were also attenuated by Tpi deficiency (Figure 8B and C).
evidence: Oxidative stress and climbing assays showing reduced benefits in PRC2 mutants with Tpi deficiency.

claim: Tpi deficiency reduces glycolysis in PRC2 mutants as shown by decreased ATP, NADH/NAD+, and GSH/(GSH+GSSG) ratios.
source: Lowering Tpi in PRC2 mutants slightly decreased the expression of Tpi gene (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E) and diminished the extent by which glycolysis could be stimulated as having relatively reduced ATP and NADH/NAD+ ratio (Figure 8D).
evidence: Metabolite measurements showing reduced glycolytic activity in PRC2 mutants with Tpi deficiency.

claim: Pgi deficiency diminishes the pro-lifespan benefits mediated by PRC2-deficiency.
source: Consistently, while Pgic392 heterozygote alone had minimal effect on aging (Figure 8—figure supplement 1F–1I), triple mutants combining Pgic392 heterozygote with Pclc421 Su(z)12c253 diminished the pro-lifespan benefits mediated by PRC2-deficiency (Figure 8E–8H, Figure 8—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Lifespan and fitness assays showing reduced benefits in PRC2 mutants with Pgi deficiency.

claim: Tpi protein levels decrease with age in WT flies.
source: Western blot analysis manifested that both Tpi and Pgi proteins had a modest decrease with age, but became upregulated upon PRC2-deficiency, an outcome consistent with the alteration in the level of H3K27me3 (Figure 9A–9D).
evidence: Western blot data showing decreased Tpi protein with age.

claim: Pgi protein levels decrease with age in WT flies.
source: Western blot analysis manifested that both Tpi and Pgi proteins had a modest decrease with age, but became upregulated upon PRC2-deficiency, an outcome consistent with the alteration in the level of H3K27me3 (Figure 9A–9D).
evidence: Western blot data showing decreased Pgi protein with age.

claim: Tpi protein levels are upregulated in PRC2 mutants.
source: Western blot analysis manifested that both Tpi and Pgi proteins had a modest decrease with age, but became upregulated upon PRC2-deficiency, an outcome consistent with the alteration in the level of H3K27me3 (Figure 9A–9D).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased Tpi protein in PRC2 mutants.

claim: Pgi protein levels are upregulated in PRC2 mutants.
source: Western blot analysis manifested that both Tpi and Pgi proteins had a modest decrease with age, but became upregulated upon PRC2-deficiency, an outcome consistent with the alteration in the level of H3K27me3 (Figure 9A–9D).
evidence: Western blot data showing increased Pgi protein in PRC2 mutants.

claim: Transgenic increase of both Tpi and Pgi genes stimulates glycolysis as shown by elevated pyruvate, ATP, and NADH/NAD+ ratio.
source: While single transgenes had modest phenotypes, animals combining both Tpi and Pgi transgenes stimulated glycolysis, as shown by elevated pyruvate, ATP, and NADH/NAD+ ratio as compared to age-matched WT (Figure 9E).
evidence: Metabolite measurements showing increased glycolytic activity in flies with Tpi and Pgi transgenes.

claim: Transgenic increase of Tpi and Pgi genes improves lifespan, locomotion, and resistance to oxidative stress.
source: Accordingly, adult aging phenotypes, including lifespan (Figure 9F), locomotion (Figure 9G), and resistance to oxidative stress (Figure 9H), were improved.
evidence: Lifespan, climbing, and oxidative stress assays showing improved phenotypes in flies with Tpi and Pgi transgenes.

claim: H3K27me3 is a signature histone modification marked and maintained by Polycomb Repressive Complexes (PRCs).
source: H3K27me3, a highly conserved histone modification signifying transcriptional repression, is marked and maintained by Polycomb Repressive Complexes (PRCs).
evidence: Statement in the abstract establishing the role of PRCs in H3K27me3 regulation.

claim: Tri-methylated histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3) denotes transcriptional silencing.
source: Tri-methylated histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3) denotes transcriptional silencing, which is produced by PRC2 (Czermin et al., 2002; Müller et al., 2002) and functionally maintained by PRC1 (Cao et al., 2002).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to previous research.

claim: H3K27me3 is produced by PRC2.
source: Tri-methylated histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3) denotes transcriptional silencing, which is produced by PRC2 (Czermin et al., 2002; Müller et al., 2002) and functionally maintained by PRC1 (Cao et al., 2002).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Czermin et al., 2002 and Müller et al., 2002.

claim: H3K27me3 is functionally maintained by PRC1.
source: Tri-methylated histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3) denotes transcriptional silencing, which is produced by PRC2 (Czermin et al., 2002; Müller et al., 2002) and functionally maintained by PRC1 (Cao et al., 2002).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Cao et al., 2002.

claim: H3K27me3 levels are known to increase with age.
source: Importantly, H3K27me3 levels are known to increase with age (Liu et al., 2013; Sun et al., 2014)
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Liu et al., 2013 and Sun et al., 2014.

claim: Glycolysis is the first step in the breakdown of glucose to extract energy in the form of ATP for cellular metabolism.
source: Glycolysis, the first step in the breakdown of glucose to extract energy in the form of ATP for cellular metabolism, is present in all cellular organisms and critical for life.
evidence: Statement describing the fundamental role of glycolysis.

claim: The anti-aging effect of caloric restriction correlates with a metabolic feature of limiting glucose metabolism including a reduction of glycolysis.
source: The anti-aging effect of caloric restriction correlates with a metabolic feature of limiting glucose metabolism including a reduction of glycolysis (Feuers et al., 1989).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Feuers et al., 1989.

claim: Decreased brain glucose metabolism is present prior to the onset of clinic symptoms in individuals at risk of Alzheimer's disease.
source: Strikingly, decreased brain glucose metabolism is present prior to the onset of clinic symptoms in individuals at risk of Alzheimer's disease (Cunnane et al., 2011).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Cunnane et al., 2011.

claim: Aging is the most significant factor for human neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Since aging is the most significant factor for human neurodegenerative diseases, it is important to better understand how glycolysis is modulated with age and whether modulation of glycolytic process could impact adult lifespan.
evidence: Statement establishing the relationship between aging and neurodegenerative diseases.

claim: Epigenetic drift of H3K27me3 is one of the molecular mechanisms that contribute to aging.
source: Our data presented in this study are consistent with the model that epigenetic drift of H3K27me3 is one of the molecular mechanisms that contribute to at least a subset of age-associated phenotypes and limit lifespan in Drosophila.
evidence: Conclusion statement based on the study's findings.

claim: A reduction of H3K27me3 by PRC2-deficiency stimulates glycolysis and healthy lifespan.
source: Moreover, we reveal that a reduction of H3K27me3 by PRC2-deficiency stimulates glycolysis and healthy lifespan.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: During natural aging, stimulation of glycolysis promotes metabolic health and longevity.
source: Our study proposes that, during natural aging, stimulation of glycolysis promotes metabolic health and longevity.
evidence: Conclusion statement proposing a mechanism based on the study's findings.

claim: Adult-onset fidelity loss results in epigenetic drift of H3K27me3.
source: Using Drosophila, we discover that adult-onset fidelity loss results in epigenetic drift of H3K27me3, which in turn impinges on the transcription and metabolism of the glycolytic pathway.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's main finding.

claim: Epigenetic drift of H3K27me3 impinges on the transcription and metabolism of the glycolytic pathway.
source: Using Drosophila, we discover that adult-onset fidelity loss results in epigenetic drift of H3K27me3, which in turn impinges on the transcription and metabolism of the glycolytic pathway.
evidence: Summary statement describing the mechanistic link discovered in the study.

claim: Perturbing glycolysis diminishes the pro-lifespan benefits mediated by PRCs-deficiency.
source: While perturbing glycolysis diminishes the pro-lifespan benefits mediated by PRCs-deficiency, transgenic increase of glycolytic genes in wild-type animals extends longevity.
evidence: Summary statement from the abstract describing experimental findings.

claim: Transgenic increase of glycolytic genes in wild-type animals extends longevity.
source: While perturbing glycolysis diminishes the pro-lifespan benefits mediated by PRCs-deficiency, transgenic increase of glycolytic genes in wild-type animals extends longevity.
evidence: Summary statement from the abstract describing experimental findings.

claim: Changes in histone markings substantially impact adult lifespan in various model organisms.
source: Previous studies have established that changes in histone markings, such as acetylation on histone H4 at lysine 16 (H4K16ac) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Dang et al., 2009), trimethylation on histone H3 at lysine 4 (H3K4me3) in Caenorhabditis elegans (Han et al., 2017), and trimethylation on histone H3 at lysine 36 (H3K36me3) in S. cerevisiae, C. elegans and Drosophila melanogaster substantially impact adult lifespan (Pu et al., 2015; Sen et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Polycomb repressive complexes (PRCs) are evolutionally conserved from the worm to Drosophila and mammals.
source: Polycomb repressive complexes (PRCs), including PRC1 (Shao et al., 1999) and PRC2 (Kuzmichev et al., 2002), are important histone-modifying enzymes (Czermin et al., 2002; Müller et al., 2002; Saurin et al., 2001) that are evolutionally conserved from the worm to Drosophila and mammals (Whitcomb et al., 2007).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Whitcomb et al., 2007.

claim: Mutation in the H3K27me3 demethylase couples an increase of H3K27me3 with longevity in C. elegans.
source: Although mutation in the H3K27me3 demethylase couples an increase of H3K27me3 with longevity in C.elegans (Jin et al., 2011; Maures et al., 2011)
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Jin et al., 2011 and Maures et al., 2011.

claim: Reducing H3K27me3 by heterozygous mutation in the H3K27me3 methyltransferase results in lifespan extension in both C. elegans and D. melanogaster.
source: reducing H3K27me3 by heterozygous mutation in the H3K27me3 methyltransferase results in lifespan extension in both C. elegans and D. melanogaster (Ni et al., 2012; Siebold et al., 2010).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Ni et al., 2012 and Siebold et al., 2010.

claim: Metabolic homeostasis is intimately connected with aging and lifespan regulation.
source: Metabolic homeostasis is intimately connected with aging and lifespan regulation (López-Otín et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to López-Otín et al., 2016.

claim: Glucose is the dominant provider of energy for cells.
source: Glucose is the dominant provider of energy for cells.
evidence: Statement describing fundamental cellular metabolism.

claim: Glycolysis is essentially involved in a wide-range of biological processes.
source: On the other hand, glycolysis is essentially involved in a wide-range of biological processes (Chang et al., 2013; Okamoto et al., 2001; Volkenhoff et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Chang et al., 2013; Okamoto et al., 2001; Volkenhoff et al., 2015.

claim: The Drosophila Utx gene catalyzes the removal of methyl groups from H3K27me3.
source: The Drosophila Utx gene has been previously implicated in catalyzing the removal of methyl groups from H3K27me3 (Smith et al., 2008)
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Smith et al., 2008.

claim: Lactate is a specific indicator for anaerobic glycolysis.
source: In particular, lactate, a specific indicator for anaerobic glycolysis (Schurr and Payne, 2007)
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Schurr and Payne, 2007.

claim: NADPH/NADP+ ratio is an indicator of the pentose phosphate pathway, foliate metabolism, and malic enzyme.
source: On the other hand, the ratio of NADPH/NADP+, an indicator of the PPP, foliate metabolism, and malic enzyme (Fan et al., 2014)
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Fan et al., 2014.

claim: Glutathione is an important indicator of the cellular redox state.
source: In parallel, we also examined the glutathione, an important indicator of the cellular redox state (Jones, 2006).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Jones, 2006.

claim: Tpi gene encodes triosephosphate isomerase, a central glycolytic enzyme.
source: Tpi gene, encoding triosephosphate isomerase, is a central glycolytic enzyme (Bar-Even et al., 2012).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Bar-Even et al., 2012.

claim: Mammalian glycolytic genes have been shown as PRCs targets.
source: Importantly, mammalian glycolytic genes have also been shown as PRCs targets (Brookes et al., 2012).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Brookes et al., 2012.

claim: Aging is characterized by the progressive decline in cellular and organismal functions that lead to reduction of fitness and increased risks to diseases and death.
source: Aging is characterized by the progressive decline in cellular and organismal functions that lead to reduction of fitness and increased risks to diseases and death.
evidence: Introductory statement defining aging.

claim: Epigenetic alterations in histone modification represent a prominent hallmark of aging.
source: Epigenetic alterations in histone modification represent a prominent hallmark of aging (Sen et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Sen et al., 2016.

claim: Chromatin and epigenetic complexes that modify histones regulate the accessibility of DNA to transcriptional machinery.
source: Chromatin and epigenetic complexes that modify histones regulate the accessibility of DNA to transcriptional machinery, thereby permitting direct control of gene expression (Kouzarides, 2007).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Kouzarides, 2007.

claim: The accumulation of ROS is the leading proposed cause of decline in cellular function and integrity in aging.
source: The accumulation of ROS is the leading proposed cause of decline in cellular function and integrity in aging (Balaban et al., 2005).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Balaban et al., 2005.

claim: Aging couples with a decline of fidelity in H3K27me3 modification, as demonstrated by a genome-wide drift of this repressive mark.
source: Our quantitative assessment shows that aging couples with a decline of fidelity in H3K27me3 modification, as demonstrated by a genome-wide drift of this repressive mark.
evidence: Summary statement of the study's main finding in the Discussion.

claim: Age-associated DNA damage reduces the fidelity of epigenetic markings.
source: One possible reason is age-associated DNA damage that reduces the fidelity of epigenetic markings. It has been well-established that aging is associated with the accumulation of DNA damage (Lu et al., 2004).
evidence: Speculative statement about mechanism supported by citation to Lu et al., 2004.

claim: UV-C irradiation can induce the increase of H3K27me3 mediated by PRC2 in Bombyx mori.
source: In Bombyx mori, UV-C irradiation can induce the increase of H3K27me3 mediated by PRC2 (Li et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Li et al., 2014.

claim: In Neurospora crassa, the increase and redistribution of H3K27me3 can be induced by the loss of H3K9 methyltransferase complex.
source: In Neurospora crassa, on the other hand, the increase and redistribution of H3K27me3 can be induced by the loss of H3K9 methyltransferase complex (Basenko et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Basenko et al., 2015.

claim: Dysregulation of H3K27me3 may be due to feed-forward interactions between DNA damage and changes in the levels of complexes that control epigenetic markings during aging.
source: Thus, dysregulation of H3K27me3 may be due to feed-forward interactions between DNA damage and changes in the levels of complexes that control epigenetic markings during aging.
evidence: Speculative statement about mechanism based on inference from cited studies.

claim: Impairing glycolysis can extend lifespan perhaps by triggering compensatory processes.
source: Previous data implicates that impairing glycolysis can extend lifespan perhaps by triggering compensatory processes (Schulz et al., 2007).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Schulz et al., 2007.

claim: Aging correlates with an increased abundance of proteins in glycolysis in mouse heart.
source: Quantitative proteomic analysis in mouse heart shows that aging correlates with an increased abundance of proteins in glycolysis, and that caloric restriction and rapamycin treatment known to extend longevity can reverse this trend (Dai et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Dai et al., 2014.

claim: D-Glucosamine supplementation that impairs glucose metabolism can extend lifespan in C. elegans and mouse.
source: D-Glucosamine supplementation that impairs glucose metabolism can extend lifespan in C. elegans and mouse (Weimer et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Weimer et al., 2014.

claim: Rat models supplemented with 2-deoxyglucose, a known anti-glycolytic compound, are short-lived.
source: However, rat models supplemented with 2-deoxyglucose, a known anti-glycolytic compound, are instead short-lived (Minor et al., 2010).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Minor et al., 2010.

claim: Glucose-enriched diet can prevent pathophysiological decline and early death of telomere dysfunctional mice by stimulating glucose metabolism including glycolysis.
source: Moreover, glucose-enriched diet can prevent pathophysiological decline and early death of telomere dysfunctional mice by stimulating glucose metabolism including glycolysis (Missios et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Missios et al., 2014.

claim: A balanced diet from protein to carbohydrate and their interactive effects are key elements for healthy longevity.
source: Importantly, recent evidence from studies on a wide range of species suggests that a balanced diet from protein to carbohydrate and their interactive effects are key elements for healthy longevity.
evidence: Summary statement of dietary research findings.

claim: Mouse dietary studies have demonstrated that animals fed on diets that are low in protein and high in carbohydrate enjoy longer life with lower blood pressure, improved glucose tolerance and lipid profiles.
source: Mouse dietary studies have demonstrated that animals fed on diets that are low in protein and high in carbohydrate enjoy longer life with lower blood pressure, improved glucose tolerance and lipid profiles (Solon-Biet et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Solon-Biet et al., 2014.

claim: Human data supports the deleterious effects of diets with high protein and low-carbohydrate.
source: This is also supported by human data on the deleterious effects of diets with high protein and low-carbohydrate (Floegel and Pischon, 2012; Lagiou et al., 2012).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Floegel and Pischon, 2012 and Lagiou et al., 2012.

claim: Enhancing NAD+ biogenesis promotes healthy lifespan.
source: It has been well-established that enhancing NAD+ biogenesis promotes healthy lifespan (Anderson et al., 2002; Balan et al., 2008; Mills et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Anderson et al., 2002; Balan et al., 2008; Mills et al., 2016.

claim: Supplementation of NAD+ precursors profoundly elevates energy metabolism by increasing the expression of genes in the TCA cycle as well as glycolysis in C. elegans.
source: As noted, supplementation of NAD+ precursors profoundly elevates energy metabolism by increasing the expression of genes in the TCA cycle as well as glycolysis in C. elegans (Mouchiroud et al., 2013)
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Mouchiroud et al., 2013.

claim: NAD+ precursors promote glucose metabolism with increased flux through pentose phosphate and glycolytic pathways in mice on a high-fat diet.
source: and promotes glucose metabolism with increased flux through pentose phosphate and glycolytic pathways in mice on a high-fat diet (Mitchell et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Mitchell et al., 2018.

claim: Declining intracellular NAD+ and thus increased NADH/NAD+ ratio correlate with aging.
source: Intriguingly, while declining intracellular NAD+ and thus increased NADH/NAD+ ratio correlate with aging (Zhu et al., 2015)
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2015.

claim: The oxidative phosphorylation, although produces more ATP than glycolysis, can yield intracellular ROS.
source: The oxidative phosphorylation, although produces more ATP than glycolysis, can yield intracellular ROS.
evidence: Statement describing metabolic processes.

claim: Modulating H3K27me3 may reprogram bioenergetic decline during aging, which in effect reduces cellular damage and deterioration.
source: Thus, modulating H3K27me3 may reprogram bioenergetic decline during aging, which in effect reduces cellular damage and deterioration.
evidence: Inference based on the study's findings about H3K27me3 and metabolism.
